title: Pipelines and Interceptors
readerIntent: Understand configurable ordered execution and explicit lifecycle extension points.
priorKnowledge: Know services and the operation lifecycle.
owner: Nodics pipeline engine and each capability's pipeline definitions
summary: Pipelines coordinate bounded technical steps; interceptors extend declared lifecycle points; durable business processes belong to workflow modules.

sections.heading: What is Pipelines and Interceptors?
paragraphs: A pipeline is an ordered series of processing steps, and an interceptor runs governed logic before or after a defined operation. Nodics uses these mechanisms to compose reusable technical behavior such as validation, security, transformation, and response handling.
Think of an airport journey with ordered checkpoints. Each checkpoint owns one responsibility, the sequence is explicit, and a rejected checkpoint prevents unsafe continuation.

sections.heading: When to use what
items: Use a service for small cohesive behavior.
Use a pipeline when ordered replaceable steps, shared context, and error traceability are part of the contract.
Use an interceptor to add behavior at a declared lifecycle point.
Use workflow for durable business state, waiting, human and automatic actions, retries across time, and business-visible lifecycle.

sections.heading: Value
items: Customize a step without copying the entire operation.
Make order, context, success, failure, and diagnostics explicit.
Reuse save, search, import, job, and governance execution patterns.
Trace failures to pipeline, instance, node, module, tenant, and safe cause.

sections.heading: Pipeline anatomy
items: Success, error, skip, and terminal transitions.
Timeout, retry, side-effect, and compensation metadata.

sections.heading: Interceptor anatomy
paragraphs: An interceptor runs at a declared lifecycle point, such as before or after save. It adds bounded behavior without copying the whole process. Order, input, output, failure, and side effects are explicit.
It is not a hidden service locator or permission to mutate unrelated capability state.

sections.heading: Pipeline versus workflow
paragraphs: A pipeline is normally bounded technical execution within one runtime operation. A workflow is durable business state that may wait for people, timers, systems, or retries across restarts.
Content approval belongs to Workflow; request parsing and schema-save processing are pipeline concerns.

sections.heading: Examples and limits
paragraphs: The request pipeline checks exposure, authentication, authorization, normalization, dispatch, and response. A save pipeline validates, persists, then triggers derived effects after success.
Do not keep durable approval state only in memory. Bound context, time, parallelism, and retries; make external effects idempotent or compensatable.

sections.heading: Customize and extend safely
paragraphs: A project first identifies the existing pipeline or interceptor lifecycle that owns the behavior. It contributes the smallest ordered node or interceptor through the supported module layer, declares its inputs, outputs, ordering, side effects, and failure contract, and leaves the base definition authoritative.

Positive, negative, boundary, ordering, timeout, duplicate-delivery, rollback, and regression tests prove that the extension changes only its intended project. Creating a second execution engine or invoking internal nodes directly would bypass governance and is not a supported customization.
